age.evidence: Ninety male, adult Sprague-Dawley rats (275-300 g) were obtained from Charles River

dosing.doses_raw: low (0.1 mg/kg), medium (1.0 mg/kg), and high (5.0 mg/kg)
dosing.evidence: Three doses of psilocybin dissolved in sterile saline (0.9%) were used: low (0.1 mg/kg), medium (1.0 mg/kg), and high (5.0 mg/kg)... Treatments were for 27 consecutive weekdays

handling.evidence: Animals were familiarized to handlers through being weighed every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday for at least 30 days prior to drug treatment.

group_housing.evidence: Rats were randomly housed in pairs in large polycarbonate cages

day_night_flipped.evidence: in a reverse-light cycle, temperature-controlled (22 °C) room

enrichment_housing.evidence: Enrichment items in the home cage are not mentioned

assays.assay_name: Home Cage Food Intake and Body Weight Monitoring
assays.assay_description: Daily measurement of body weight and high-calorie cafeteria diet consumption in home cage over 27 weekday treatment days in rats fed a cafeteria diet.

application_type.evidence: an intraperitoneal (IP) injection of saline or the dose of psilocybin (0.1, 1, and 5 mg/kg)

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats were randomly housed in pairs in large polycarbonate cages

food_restriction.evidence: given ad libitum access to both the rat-chow and the cafeteria diet

time_to_assay.evidence: body weights and high calorie food intake were recorded daily across 27 weekday treatments

outcomes.summary: Chronic psilocybin (0.1 and 5 mg/kg, i.p.) significantly reduced relative body weight gain over 27 weekdays compared to vehicle-treated high-calorie diet controls; metformin (300 mg/kg p.o.) produced an even greater reduction. High-dose psilocybin and metformin also reduced high-calorie food consumption, most pronounced in the first 2 weeks.
outcomes.statistics: Weight gain: F(4,68)=6.92, p<0.001; main effect of time F(26,1768)=261.359, p<0.001; drug×time F(104,1768)=3.391, p<0.001; low dose vs control p<0.05; high dose vs control p<0.01. Food consumption: F(3,55)=1.990, p=0.126; days 1-6 F(4,73)=3.12, p<0.01.
outcomes.evidence: Both the low and high dose psilocybin groups caused a significant decrease in changes in body weight compared to controls... Both high dose psilocybin and metformin decreased consumption of the high calorie diet

B1_num_measures.evidence: body weights and high calorie food intake were recorded daily; Consumption was also analyzed based on caloric content

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: follow-up analysis of relative food consumption in shorter time bins (days 1-6, 7-13, 14-19, and 20-27)

B4_ethological.evidence: voluntarily fed a high calorie 'cafeteria' diet; feeding behaviour measured

B5_social.evidence: Assay does not target social behaviour

B7_automated_classification.evidence: leftover diet food was removed and weighed daily (manual measurement)

B8_multivariate.evidence: Pearson correlations and ANOVAs; no PCA/multivariate analysis

E1_environment_type.evidence: Rats were randomly housed in pairs in large polycarbonate cages; food consumption measured in home cage

E3_bedding.evidence: Standard home cage housing (polycarbonate cages with bedding implied as standard rat housing)

E7_social_context.evidence: Rats were randomly housed in pairs

E8_food_water.evidence: given ad libitum access to both the rat-chow and the cafeteria diet

D1_continuity.evidence: body weights and high calorie food intake were recorded daily across 27 weekdays

D2_session_duration.evidence: leftover diet food was removed and weighed daily (24-h consumption window)

D3_recording_days.evidence: Treatments were for 27 consecutive weekdays, and body weights and high calorie food intake were recorded daily

D4_baseline.evidence: At baseline, immediately prior to drug treatment, all groups previously exposed to the cafeteria diet exhibited significantly greater weight

D5_followup.evidence: No follow-up after drug discontinuation reported

judge_notes: Two candidates (glm, gptoss) returned no assays; only qwen identified the home-cage feeding/body-weight monitoring as a behavioural assay. Kept this assay since feeding behaviour is the primary behavioural readout.
Excluded fasting glucose, IGTT, and fat-pad dissection as they are physiological/anatomical endpoints, not behavioural assays.
E3 bedding scored 1 with low confidence since rats were in standard polycarbonate home cages where bedding is conventional, though not explicitly stated.
D2 and D6 scored as >6h since daily food consumption was measured over 24-h periods, consistent with continuous home-cage monitoring.
